findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:65 — All-clients MANAGE/CONFIGURE has no exclusion for the admin-permissions and realm-management clients, so a "manage all clients" delegate can manage the client that holds every FGAP permission (including deleting it) and edit realm-management admin roles.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:65 — All-clients MANAGE/CONFIGURE has no exclusion for the admin-permissions and realm-management clients, so a "manage all clients" delegate can manage the client that holds every FGAP permission (including deleting it) and edit realm-management admin roles.

adjudication.rationale: The new V2 client permission evaluation applies the "all-clients" permission to any ClientModel without exceptions. In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when no per-client resource exists it falls back to the resource-type resource for AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("all clients") and grants if a policy exists. canManage(ClientModel) and canConfigure(ClientModel) directly rely on this (via hasPermission(client, MANAGE/CONFIGURE)) and there is no check to exclude special/internal clients (e.g., the admin-permissions client that stores FGAP policies/resources or realm-management). Thus, granting MANAGE/CONFIGURE at the clients resource-type level would also authorize managing those internal clients, which is a security/correctness risk consistent with the finding.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — The listener is now gated on the V1 feature (V1 and V2 are exclusive versions), so under V2 a deleted client's per-client resource and permissions stay behind with no cleanup, and a client later re-created with the same id inherits them.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148 — canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions and the legacy *Permission(client) methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the legacy token-exchange and client management-permissions endpoints return 500 once V2 is enabled instead of failing cleanly.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` implementation, multiple methods that are part of the existing `ClientPermissions` API are overridden to immediately throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). The diff also changes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, meaning any existing/legacy code paths or endpoints that still invoke these methods when V2 is enabled will now raise an uncaught runtime exception, which typically manifests as an HTTP 500 rather than a controlled/clean failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:83 — getOrCreateResource resolves by findById/findByName with no resource-type check, so a Clients-typed permission can attach to the "Users" all-resource or a user resource (overlapping manage/view/map-roles scopes). The flat Users/Clients name namespace also lets hasPermission(client) evaluate a same-id user resource.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new "Clients" resource type and ClientPermissionsV2 does lookup resources by name (client.getId()) without an explicit type filter, but the finding’s concrete claim that a Clients-typed permission can attach to the "Users" all-resource (name "Users") is not supported by the diff: client resources are looked up/created using the client internal id (UUID) or the literal "Clients" for the all-clients resource, neither of which overlaps with the "Users" all-resource name. Also, the alleged lack of resource-type checks in AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource’s store lookup is not shown in the provided hunks, so it can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:304 — getResourceName has no Clients branch, so client permission resources fall back to getDisplayName() (null for UUID-named resources) instead of showing the clientId or "All clients".

adjudication.rationale: The finding cites `AdminPermissionsSchema.java:304` and a `getResourceName` method lacking a Clients branch, but that method/line is not present in the provided diff, so the claim can’t be verified from what’s shown. What is verifiable is that this diff *does* add explicit client handling in `getOrCreateResource(...)` (`else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)) { name = resolveClient(session, id); }`) plus `resolveClient(...)`, so the assertion that client resources "fall back" due to having no Clients branch appears to misread the changes (at least with respect to the code shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — The map-roles test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and has no negative case for other clients, so it passes even if composite mapping works through configure or leaks across clients.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`, the permission granted to the target client includes `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`. Because `CONFIGURE` is bundled with the map-roles scopes, the test does not isolate whether `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (or `MAP_ROLES`) is actually required/enforced for the composite-mapping operation; the operation could succeed due to broader `CONFIGURE` permissions. Also, the test only asserts success on `myclient` after granting permissions and does not include a negative check attempting the same operations against a different client to ensure permissions don’t accidentally apply cross-client. This is a concrete test-coverage/validation gap shown in the diff, not a proven product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Gating the removal listener on the V1 feature means that deleting a client/role/group no longer cleans up leftover V1 permissions when V1 is off, and nothing cleans up the V2 per-client resource, so orphaned authz resources remain.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root problem: the removal/cleanup listener is incorrectly gated by the V1 feature flag, so when V2 is enabled but V1 is off, cleanup logic won’t run and authorization/permission resources are left orphaned. This matches the golden comment’s inconsistency/feature-flag-guard bug and its orphaned-permissions consequence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Cleanup on client removal now only runs under the V1 feature, and nothing replaces it for V2, so per-client resources and permissions stay behind after a client is deleted and reattach to any client re-imported with the same id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — The test grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE together, and the pre-grant failures come from the missing user map-roles and configure permissions, so it never shows that the client map-roles or map-roles-composite checks are enforced on their own.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`, after the initial expected `ForbiddenException` checks, the test grants `MAP_ROLES` on USERS plus `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)` on the client in a single step, then only verifies the operations succeed. Because the permissions are bundled (and the first operation likely depends on both user and client permissions), the test does not isolate and demonstrate that client-side `MAP_ROLES` vs `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` enforcement works independently (e.g., that granting only one still forbids the other operation). This is a concrete test-coverage gap for the newly added client scopes, not a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — No test covers the new map-roles-client-scope scope (canMapClientScopeRoles), in either the per-client or the all-clients form.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and new logic in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` that checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. However, the added/updated tests (notably `PermissionClientTest`) only exercise `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (and `CONFIGURE`, `MANAGE`, `VIEW`) and never create a permission granting `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` nor assert behavior tied to `canMapClientScopeRoles` for either a specific client or the all-clients resource type. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test coverage issue for newly added permission behavior, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:127 — There is no client test with a NEGATIVE/deny policy or a specific-client permission that overrides an all-clients permission, although UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest covers this for users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new V2 client-scope authorization logic (e.g., ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) falls back to the all-clients resource and evaluates permissions via root.evaluatePermission). PermissionClientTest adds multiple positive-path tests (manage/configure single client, manage/view all clients, map roles), but none exercise deny/NEGATIVE policy logic or the interaction between an all-clients permission and a more specific per-client permission that should override it. By contrast, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest explicitly tests a NEGATIVE permission overriding an all-users permission. Given the new fallback/all-clients behavior, lack of a corresponding client override/deny test is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:284 — View is tested only for all clients: no test covers VIEW on a single client, CONFIGURE on all clients, or MAP_ROLES on all clients (the getResourceTypeResource fallback in hasPermission).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new fine-grained client permission scopes and evaluation paths in `ClientPermissionsV2`, including (a) per-client checks like `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES...)` and (b) the per-client fallback when no client-specific `Resource` exists: `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` loads the resource-type resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and evaluates it. In `PermissionClientTest`, new coverage includes `testViewAllClients` (VIEW for all), `testManageAllClients` (MANAGE for all), and single-client tests for MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES, but there is indeed no test for VIEW on a single client, no test for CONFIGURE on all clients, and no test for MAP_ROLES on all clients (which would exercise the resource-type fallback path for those scopes). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:118 — The V2 overrides canView(ClientScopeModel) and canManageClientScopes are not tested through the /client-scopes endpoints with an all-clients VIEW/MANAGE permission.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds V2-specific logic in `ClientPermissionsV2` for `canManageClientScopes()` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (e.g., checking all-clients `MANAGE`/`VIEW` via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE|VIEW)`). The newly added/updated tests in `PermissionClientTest` exercise client endpoints like `clients().findAll()`, `clients().create()`, `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes()` and protocol mapper operations, but they do not exercise the realm `/client-scopes` endpoints (which would directly rely on `canManageClientScopes()` / `canView(ClientScopeModel)` behavior) under an all-clients VIEW/MANAGE permission created via `createAllPermission(..., clientsType, ..., Set.of(VIEW|MANAGE))`. So the finding identifies a concrete, diff-grounded missing test for new authorization logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148 — canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled and getPermissions now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2, but no test checks how token exchange or the client management/permissions endpoints behave with V2 enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` where several inherited operations now explicitly `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, and multiple `*Permission(...)` methods). The added tests focus on client view/manage/configure/map-roles behavior (`PermissionClientTest`) but do not exercise any of the endpoints/flows that would call these now-unsupported methods (e.g., token exchange-related paths or permissions-enabled/permission retrieval behaviors). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap concern rather than a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:226 — generateNewSecret rotates the secret of myclient, which realmAdminClient uses to authenticate (with "mysecret"), and the secret is never restored, so later tests in the class can break depending on run order.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testConfigureOnlyOneClient()`, the test calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` (and `invalidateRotatedSecret()`) on the `myclient` client after granting CONFIGURE. `realmAdminClient` is injected with `@InjectAdminClient(..., client = "myclient", user = "myadmin")`, so it plausibly relies on the `myclient` configuration for authentication. The diff shows no restoration of the original secret (and `@AfterEach` only removes permissions), creating a realistic risk of inter-test interference/run-order dependent failures within the class once the admin client needs to re-authenticate/refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:148 — The pre-grant negative check for removeDefaultClientScope never reaches that call, because getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) throws Forbidden first, so remove authorization is not checked.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient(), the pre-grant negative check does `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` and then `removeDefaultClientScope(...)` inside one try/catch. If `getDefaultClientScopes()` is itself forbidden (as also asserted in testConfigureOnlyOneClient’s pre-checks), the code will throw before reaching `removeDefaultClientScope`, so the test would still pass without actually asserting that the *remove* operation is denied. This is a test-assertion gap/ambiguity rather than a product defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:242 — The configure-only negative test re-adds a scope that is already a default scope, so the Forbidden result is not clearly caused by the missing manage permission.

adjudication.rationale: In `testConfigureOnlyOneClient()`, after granting only `CONFIGURE`, the negative check for adding a default client scope calls `clientResource.addDefaultClientScope(defaultClientScopes.get(0).getId())`, where `defaultClientScopes` was just obtained via `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes()`. That means it is attempting to add a scope that is already a default scope. If the endpoint behaves idempotently/no-ops when the scope is already present, the observed failure/success would not clearly demonstrate that `MANAGE` is required, making the test assertion about Forbidden potentially ambiguous.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:178 — After removing a default scope and adding it as optional, the test never checks the client's scopes, so a request that succeeds but changes nothing would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient(), after calling clientResource.removeDefaultClientScope(clientScopeRep.getId()) and then clientResource.addOptionalClientScope(clientScopeRep.getId()), the test does not verify the resulting default/optional client scope assignments (e.g., via getDefaultClientScopes()/getOptionalClientScopes()). As written, the test would still pass if these endpoints returned 2xx but failed to actually change the scope mappings, making it a concrete test-coverage gap rather than a product defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:166 — testManageOnlyOneClient permanently changes the shared myclient (its name and default/optional scopes) without cleanup, so tests in the class depend on each other.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient, the test updates the existing shared client "myclient" (myclient.setName("somethingNew"); clientResource.update(myclient);) and mutates its client-scope configuration (removeDefaultClientScope(...) and addOptionalClientScope(...)) with no corresponding cleanup/reset. The only @AfterEach cleanup shown removes authorization permissions, not client state, so subsequent tests in the class can observe modified realm state and become order-dependent/flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:334 — Client roles created on myclient, and the role mapping to myadmin, have no realm.cleanup() registration, so they leak into later tests.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient (new code near the end of the diff), the test creates two client roles on "myclient" via realm.admin().clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().create(...) and then assigns a client-level role to myadmin. The class @AfterEach only removes scope permissions (getScopePermissionsResource(client) ... remove()) and does not remove the created roles or undo the role mapping. No realm.cleanup() registration is added for these role creations/mappings, so they can persist and affect later tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:280 — The all-clients list checks use not(empty()), which would still pass if only some of the clients were visible.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest, the “all clients” assertions only check that the returned list is non-empty (e.g., `assertThat(found, not(empty()))` in `testManageAllClients()` and `testViewAllClients()` after granting all-clients permissions). This would still pass even if the API incorrectly returned only a subset of clients, so the test does not fully validate “all clients visible” behavior. This is a test coverage/strength issue rather than a product bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java:136 — The new createClientPolicy helper is never used, so client-policy-based permissions for the Clients type are untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `AbstractPermissionTest`, a new helper `createClientPolicy(...)` was added, but in the provided diff there are no call sites for it (tests like `PermissionClientTest` only create `UserPolicyRepresentation` via `createUserPolicy(...)` and then build client permissions from that). As a result, the new Clients resource-type permissions are exercised only with user-based policies, and not with client-policy-based permissions, leaving that specific path untested.
